methodological_rigor.justification: Methodological study comparing feature selection methods on TCGA breast cancer data (705 patients, 1936 features). Controlled perturbation framework (removing top feature, checking ranking consistency). Compares 7 methods (Linear Regression, LASSO, RF, XGBoost, PCA, Highly Variable Gene Selection, Spearman correlation). Main limitation: single dataset, no external validation, strict consistency metric (requiring identical rank positions) may be overly stringent, no prospective clinical validation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Methodological investigation of AI interpretability in oncology. Addresses important problem of feature importance instability but provides no direct clinical evidence or patient outcomes. Recommendations are algorithmic, not clinical.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods clearly described with parameter settings documented. Cross-validation approach detailed. TCGA data publicly available. Limitations acknowledged (single dataset, class imbalance, no GenAI use disclosed). No pre-registration. Some clarity gaps in exact perturbation procedure.

novelty_literature.justification: Feature importance stability previously discussed in literature. Subset instability (Jaccard, Kuncheva indices) critiqued in prior work. This study's contribution is applying stricter ranking-order consistency metric, confirmatory rather than novel.

writing_presentation.justification: Introduction well-motivated on interpretability-accuracy misconception. Methods clearly specified. Results present stability assessment and predictive performance side-by-side. Discussion appropriately cautious but somewhat speculative about clinical implications without clinical data.

key_strengths: Identifies important gap: high predictive accuracy does NOT guarantee stable feature importance; supervised models exhibit ranking instability under minimal perturbation (<0.1% feature removal)
Rigorous perturbation methodology: removes top-ranked feature, checks whether remaining 19 features maintain exact rank order—stricter than existing overlap-based metrics
Demonstrates that simpler unsupervised methods (Highly Variable Gene Selection, Spearman correlation) achieve competitive predictive performance with superior ranking stability
key_concerns: Single-dataset validation on TCGA breast cancer limits generalizability; no external validation in independent cohorts or other cancer types

Strict ranking consistency criterion (identical position preservation) may be overly stringent; biological relevance of small rank shifts unclear; partial stability metrics dismissed without quantitative comparison
No clinical outcome data or prospective validation; algorithmic recommendations not grounded in clinical decision-making impact
chief_reviewer.rationale: Important methodological investigation identifying feature importance instability in popular ML models. However, single-dataset design, strict metric without biological validation, and lack of clinical grounding limit impact. Tier 4 appropriate for methodological study requiring external validation and clinical relevance demonstration.
